summary: WPA3-FT/OKC rollout: Linux clients experience DHCP lease flaps and WireGuard route loss to internal services
description:
Issue summary:
After the SF office Wi‑Fi was migrated to WPA3-Enterprise with Fast Transition (FT) and Opportunistic Key Caching (OKC) the week of 2026-03-01, multiple Linux laptops (NetworkManager + wpa_supplicant) began experiencing repeated DHCP lease renewals. When the renew occurs, WireGuard tunnels on the clients lose the bound route to the internal default gateway, which results in intermittent inability to reach internal services (grafana, internal git, vault).

Impact:
- ~12 engineers across SF office report intermittent access to internal services since 2026-03-02.
- Affected users must re-establish WireGuard manually or reconnect to Wi‑Fi to restore access.
- Productivity impacted for ~20% of users on Linux workstations; Mac/Windows not observed.

Environment:
- SF office SSID: Redwood-Corp (WPA3-Enterprise, FT enabled, OKC enabled)
- Client OS seen: Ubuntu 22.04 / Fedora 37 / Debian 12 using NetworkManager 1.38+ and wpa_supplicant built with FT support
- VPN: WireGuard client (wg-quick systemd service) bound to default route via wg0
- DHCP: office DHCP server cluster (isc-dhcpd) handing option 3 (router) and option 121 sometimes via relay

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Connect an affected Linux laptop to Redwood-Corp SSID.
2. Perform continuous traffic to an internal service (e.g., tail -f logs from internal grafana via curl streaming).
3. Wait for FT roam / AP reassociation or simulated roam by toggling radio (soft block/unblock).
4. Client obtains a new DHCP lease (lease time shorter than expected) and concurrently NetworkManager updates route table.
5. WireGuard still shows interface up but default route points to new DHCP gateway; some clients lose persistence of WireGuard route and traffic to internal CIDR fails until wg-quick restart or systemd restart of wg-quick@wg0.service.

Observed behavior:
- DHCP renews every ~5-15 minutes on affected clients (unexpected; other OSes fine).
- syslog shows wpa_supplicant FT reassociation and a quick DHCP DISCOVER/REQUEST sequence.
- NetworkManager issues a routable default route update; on some clients, wg-quick does not re-apply AllowedIPs routes correctly (race condition).
- No 802.1X authentication failures seen.

Expected behavior:
- FT/OKC roam should not cause prolonged DHCP churn nor break persistent WireGuard routes.

Logs / Artifacts:
- Attachments: truncated /var/log/syslog snippets from two machines (attached in ticket), tcpdump during roam, DHCP server logs for 2026-03-02 08:00-12:00 PST, WireGuard status output from affected client.
- Relevant syslog lines: "wpa_supplicant: FT: reassociation complete" then within 1-2s "dhclient: DHCPREQUEST for x.x.x.x" then "wg-quick[xxx]: Updating AllowedIPs" followed by loss of internal connectivity.

Initial hypothesis:
- Race between NetworkManager DHCP route update and wg-quick route reconciliation after FT reassociation.
- OKC/FT causes reassociation without full interface down; DHCP client triggers a lease refresh that triggers route replacement. On Linux, wg-quick relies on pre-up/post-down hooks that may not fire on a soft roam.

Immediate impact mitigation requested:
- Temporary mitigation guidance for users and a short runbook so Support can remediate quickly when reported.
comments: 2026-03-08 09:12 — Ava Martinez: Filing after 3 reports this morning. Attached logs from two affected laptops and DHCP server window. Assigning to Networking triage.
2026-03-08 10:03 — Rohit Singh: Investigating. Initial sniff shows DHCPREQUEST immediately after FT reassoc. Can you confirm which NetworkManager and wpa_supplicant versions?

2026-03-08 11:05 — Miguel Ortega (Support): Collected additional user reports. One user (host: am-dev-07) required systemd restart of wg-quick to restore routes.
User noted auto-updates to NetworkManager 1.38 last week.

2026-03-09 08:45 — Priya Desai (SRE): Confirmed DHCP lease churn on server logs; lease_time set to 600s for vendor policy but churn appears sooner per client logs. Suspect client-side DHCP renewal request triggered on reassoc.

2026-03-10 14:20 — Ben Carter (Networking): Reproduced in lab by enabling FT on AP controller and forcing roam. Observed race where NetworkManager deletes old routes before wg-quick re-applies AllowedIPs. Creating test patch to delay route flush until post-DHCP stabilization.

2026-03-11 09:30 — Rohit Singh: Applied temporary support-runbook: (1) sudo systemctl restart wg-quick@wg0 OR (2) nmcli connection down "Wired connection 1"; nmcli connection up "Wired connection 1". This restores connectivity immediately.
Will push longer-term client config to prevent automatic route flush on soft reassoc.
2026-03-12 16:02 — Ava Martinez: Rolling out communication to SF office informing of workaround and asking affected users to open ticket if they see recurrence.
2026-03-12 16:30 — Ben Carter (Networking): Opened PR to network-config with AP FT guard timer changes and suggested client-side NetworkManager/dispatcher script to reapply wg routes. PR link above.
investigation_notes: Checked DHCP server (isc-dhcpd) logs: many clients requesting renewal immediately after FT reassociation. No server-side denies or conflicts.
Lab reproduction succeeded when enabling OKC+FT on Aruba controller and forcing roam via AP CLI. Linux NM behaved differently than macOS/Windows.
Trace of NetworkManager dispatcher: dispatcher.d is invoked but wg-quick uses ifdown/ifup style hooks that assume full link down/up; soft reassoc may not trigger expected hooks.

Observed that wg-quick does 'ip route add' of AllowedIPs at start; a subsequent 'ip route replace default via <dhcp-gw>' from dhclient can override routes leading to asymmetric routing (packets reach gateway but do not traverse wg interface).

Tested quick workaround: a small systemd unit that runs 'wg syncconf wg0 /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf' after NM reports 'carrier' restored; this re-applies correct AllowedIPs. Restores connectivity consistently in lab.
Network team experimenting with AP controller guard interval to prevent immediate reassoc on weak signal which reduces churn but does not fully eliminate it.
SRE requested logging improvements for wg-quick to log AllowedIPs reapplication events to help correlate in future incidents.
resolution: Workaround deployed: support runbook provided to affected users (systemd restart of wg-quick or temporary network connection bounce). Short-term mitigation: AP guard and DHCP tuning applied in SF office to reduce churn. Long-term fix path: (1) push NetworkManager dispatcher script that re-applies WireGuard AllowedIPs on FT/OKC events, (2) upstream discussion with NetworkManager maintainers about soft-reassoc hook behavior, (3) evaluate changing wg-quick to a persistent routing reconciler or adopt wgctrl-based service. PR created in infra repo for client-side dispatcher; monitoring set up to track recurrence for 2 weeks.
next_steps: Merge and deploy network-config PR to AP controllers (Ben) — target: 2026-03-16
Ship NetworkManager dispatcher script via autoupdate to Linux fleet (Rohit) — target: 2026-03-20
Follow up with NetworkManager upstream with repro case (Priya) — target: 2026-03-22
Monitor incident channel #net-incident for new reports; close ticket after 14 days without recurrence.
